name: Nagahara
tagline: Shibuya in 24 minutes and Shinagawa in 25 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000.
summary: The station is in Ota City, served by Tokyu Ikegami Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 37 minutes to Otemachi, 33 minutes to Shinjuku, 24 minutes to Shibuya and 25 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. The station stands 33.7 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 14.7 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 33.7 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 21.6 m to 36.3 m, a difference of 14.7 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, neither the station nor any of the nine points within 400 m of it falls inside the projected inundation area. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.

groceries.name: まいばすけっと 長原駅前店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 15 clinics and 10 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is おきの会旗の台病院, about 3 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 昭和医科大学病院, about 14 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyu Ikegami Line.
congestion: Tokyu Ikegami Line runs at 130% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 大崎広小路→五反田, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥80,000 to ¥90,000 and 1K ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. 1LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 2LDK ¥220,000 to ¥230,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. a small projected flood depth and schools and parks within walking distance pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Hatanodai is ahead on rail connections and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Nagahara. Hatanodai also has the Tokyu Oimachi Line, which Nagahara does not. With more lines, Hatanodai is the better connected of the two. To Shinagawa, for instance, Hatanodai is 7 minutes quicker. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

neighbours.lead: For how close the centre is, Kita-Senzoku; for lower rent, Nagahara.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Nagahara. Kita-Senzoku has the Tokyu Oimachi Line, a different set from Nagahara. To Shinagawa, for instance, Kita-Senzoku is 5 minutes quicker. A one-room flat costs about ¥6,000 more at Kita-Senzoku. On how easy the shopping is, Nagahara comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 11 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 1 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Neither the station nor the ground around it falls inside the projected flood area.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyu Ikegami Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are lightly loaded in the morning.
